 558 of 764 pass the November 2026 aeronautical engineers exam; a Holy Angel graduate tops it
 Only 558 of 764 examinees passed the November 2026 aeronautical engineers board exam. A Holy Angel University graduate posted the top score of 92.65 percent, and WCC North Manila was the best school! #AeronauticalEngineering #PRC #BoardExam #Philippines #Aviation
 by 
 ASTIG PR 
 7 hours ago 7 hours ago 
 Advertisements 
 More than 200 aspiring aeronautical engineers did not make it. The Professional Regulation Commission announced that 558 of 764 examinees passed the November 2026 Aeronautical Engineers Computer-Based Licensure Examination.
 That is a passing rate of about 73 percent, computed from the two figures the commission released. The results came out one working day after the last day of testing.
 A Holy Angel graduate took the top score
 A graduate of Holy Angel University in Angeles City posted the highest score at 92.65 percent, GMA News reported. The commission’s own results bulletin does not carry a topnotcher’s name or score.
 WCC Aeronautical and Technical College-North Manila was the best-performing school among those with 50 or more examinees, with 51 of 56 passing, GMA News reported. That works out to about 91 percent for that school.
 Where the exam was given
 The Board of Aeronautical Engineering administered the test in Metro Manila, Cagayan de Oro, Cebu, Davao, Legazpi, Lucena, Pampanga and Rosales.
 The board was chaired by Ernesto B. Ferreras, with Redentor C. Malia as member.

 Registration opens

 What passers do next
 Registration for the Professional Identification Card and the Certificate of Registration will be done online starting Dec. 10, 2026, through the commission’s website. Passers are told to follow the posted instructions and to bring the documents the commission lists, beginning with a screenshot of the system-generated registration form.
 The commission said the date and venue of the oathtaking ceremony will be announced later. 
 A small, specialised cycle
 Aeronautical engineering is one of the commission’s smaller licensure cycles. By comparison, 10,746 candidates took the October 2026 accountancy exam and 2,337 took the October 2026 electronics engineers exam , both reported earlier.
 The November cycle has also produced results for other professions. The commission released the veterinarians licensure exam earlier this week, with 1,083 of 1,503 passing, and the midwives licensure exam with 1,343 of 2,632.
 Why the licence matters
 Aeronautical engineers work on aircraft design, airworthiness, maintenance programmes and aviation safety, a licensed field tied directly to the country’s airlines, maintenance providers and aerospace locators.
 How much the licence is worth in the job market is a separate question. A study by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies found that for education graduates, holding a professional licence does not automatically raise pay , and that job matching matters more.
